evidence: The transfer from the generating inequality to power sums and other penalties is a known general principle. Rajan & Tepedelenlioglu (IEEE TIT 61(4):1619-1628, 2015; arXiv 1302.5383) define the "ergodic capacity order" (Def. 1): X <=_c Y iff E log(1+rho X) <= E log(1+rho Y) for all rho >= 0. Their Property S1 states "X <=_c Y <=> E[g(X)] <= E[g(Y)] for all g in TBF", where TBF is the Thorin-Bernstein class g(x) = a + bx + int log(1+x/s) mu(ds) (their eq. 6). The proof of Property M1 (App. A, eqs. 28-31) matches ours step for step: take rho -> 0 for the linear term, then integrate log(1+t rho x) against a positive measure. Applied to the empirical measure of x (zero padding is allowed because a=0), it gives Remark "other penalties" verbatim, and Lemma cost at 0<r<1 is the case g = x^r. The class psi = cx + int log(1+xt) mu(dt) is exactly the Thorin-Bernstein functions vanishing at 0, which is Schilling-Song-Vondracek, Bernstein Functions, de Gruyter Studies in Math 37, Ch. 8 (1st-ed. TOC fetched; Ch. 8 starts p. 73). Lemma bernstein (the integral formula for x^r) is a standard Beta-integral representation. Going from e_k >= binom(nu,k) to prod(1+x t) >= (1+t)^nu is trivial because all coefficients are nonnegative. Searches of majorization work (power majorization, Cuttler-Greene-Skandera, trumping) found nothing closer. We found no prior statement of the chain lemma (the sign constraints JF force H = sum beta_l m_l m_l^* to be upper triangular with constant diagonal) or of its consequence e_k(|nu beta|) >= binom(nu,k) with the orthogonal equality case, obtained via Sylvester, minor expansion and Hadamard. That part is ours; its tools are textbook. Queries run: Thorin-Bernstein representation (Schilling Song Vondracek); elementary symmetric e_k domination implies fractional power sums via log(1+tx). recommended_citations.why: Supports the transfer step in Remark 'other penalties' and in the proof of Lemma cost. Property S1: domination of E log(1+rho X) for all rho is equivalent to domination of E g(X) for every Thorin-Bernstein g. The proof in App. A (eqs. 28-31) is the same integration argument we use.

Ch. 8 (Thorin-Bernstein functions) gives the representation a + bx + int log(1+x/s) mu(ds). This names the class psi in Remark 'other penalties' and is the standard reference for the integral representation of x^r in Lemma bernstein.
